newsitem.title: UK: British Conservatives elect Hague as new leader.
newsitem.headline: British Conservatives elect Hague as new leader.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Conservative party on Thursday elected former Welsh secretary William Hague as its new leader to succeed former prime minister John Major.
Officials announced that in a ballot of the Conservatives' 164 members of parliament, Hague won 92 votes against 70 for ex-finance minister Kenneth Clarke, his sole remaining challenger.
Major announced his decision to step down as leader within hours of the Conservatives' crushing defeat in the May 1 election at the hands of Tony Blair's Labour party.
Hague, 36, clinched victory after winning the backing late on Wednesday of former prime minister Margaret Thatcher, the standard-bearer of the party's right wing.
